papers.title: The Effects of Jargon on Processing Fluency, Self-Perceptions, and Scientific Engagement
papers.study_kind: Randomized 2×2 between-subjects experiment with observational serial mediation
papers.scope: Full extracted paper pp.1–19, including methods, results, limitations, stimuli and references; actual DOI and year from p.1.
papers.sample_and_design: 650 paid U.S. Qualtrics panel adults randomized to jargon/no jargon and optional mouseover definitions/no definitions; each read three same-condition short science-technology passages (autonomous cars, surgical robots, 3D bioprinting). Jargon had 10 terms per paragraph; no-jargon replaced terms with explanations/synonyms; within-topic word counts held constant (pp.6–8).
papers.outcomes: Self-reported 1–7 processing fluency, science/technology self-schema, interest, information-seeking intention, internal efficacy, perceived knowledge. Not objective comprehension or actual behavior.
limitations: Short, controlled, text-only immediate exposures; paid U.S. panel is not all audiences.
Definition treatment only offered hover access; 109/330 used by self-report. Findings do not show inline definitions are ineffective.
No objective understanding test; causal jargon manipulation does not identify causal serial mediation.
Appendix stimuli include technical claims that should not be treated as verified facts.
papers.data_or_code_leads: Online supplemental scale items mentioned p.8; no verified dataset or software release in full text.
extraction_issues: Paper describes 109 as 31% of 330; calculation is approximately 33%, retain original numerator and denominator.
Table 1 repeats some jargon cells unusually; do not use suspect topic rows for independent calculation.
papers.review_scope: Strategy-use verification of selected decisive passages; specialist review supplies full-paper extraction.

findings.claim: Lower reported processing fluency under jargon and no significant definition-condition mitigation; optional mouseover access does not test inline teaching or establish objective comprehension.
findings.evidence_locator: Methods, Results and limitations: jargon and definition conditions; active use of mouseover; immediate and cross-sectional measures.
findings.denominator: No new numeric effect estimate in this strategic finding; see specialist record for original study units.
findings.interpretation_limits: Scoped study result or pedagogical implication; not a test of this plugin.

papers.title: When curiosity gaps backfire: effects of headline concreteness on information selection decisions
papers.study_kind: Registered report; multilevel meta-analysis of randomized field package tests with observational feature moderator
papers.scope: English Upworthy 2013–2015 article headline/image previews; website visitors; clicks per impression. Individual knowledge, curiosity, comprehension and quality not measured.
papers.sample_and_design: Pilot followed by held-out confirmatory archive subset; split image-varying tests into one-image bundles, retain bundles with at least two scorable distinct headlines; binomial random-intercept/slope model for headline score nested within test; mean test concreteness interacts with within-test deviation. Randomized assignment is to complete packages, not controlled random assignment of concreteness or mean test concreteness. Same original test may yield multiple image bundles.
outcomes: CTR on a preview, not article comprehension or durable engagement
concreteness proxy validated against mean human ratings
limitations: Score uses lexical concreteness, NER assigns entities maximum, excludes headlines with unmatched words ≥3 characters; removes 17.1% of headlines (p4).
Same article A/B estimates causal package contrasts but not causal interventions on concreteness or the cross-test average; inference rests on model and unmeasured co-varying features.
US English audience, one publisher, editorial selection and historical algorithm environment; no individual-level curiosity measurement.
p5 defines CTR backwards as impressions/clicks; p3 correctly defines clicks/impressions; p8 prose contradicts low/high example direction and values 4.37 versus 4.41.
data_or_code_leads: https://osf.io/fbzvw/ (paper analysis code; not independently audited)
https://github.com/maubinle/sentence_concreteness (paper names package; no install or license audit)
https://upworthy.natematias.com (archive access on request per p10)
extraction_issues: p5 inverse CTR formula contradicts p3; p6 pilot/confirmatory wording inconsistency; p8 upper-bound example reverses score descriptions.
papers.review_scope: Strategy-use verification of selected decisive passages; specialist review supplies full-paper extraction.

findings.claim: Headline-concreteness associations with click-through vary with baseline; the paper does not establish a universal concrete-writing optimum.
findings.evidence_locator: Abstract and Discussion/limitations: direction depends on baseline and sampled Upworthy audience.
findings.denominator: No new numeric effect estimate in this strategic finding; see specialist record for original study units.
findings.interpretation_limits: Scoped study result or pedagogical implication; not a test of this plugin.

papers.title: Use of Promotional Language in Grant Applications and Grant Success
papers.study_kind: cross-sectional observational association study with regression and lexical validation
papers.scope: Biomedical grant applications to NNF in 2015–2022 and Northwestern faculty NIH submissions in 2007–2019; funded and rejected full application texts. Audience includes agency reviewers, not general workplace decision makers.
papers.sample_and_design: 9,096 NNF applications, 2,439 NIH applications from one university; dictionary fraction of 139 science-specific promotional words, logistic association with covariates including applicant performance and grant features and year/length fixed effects. Lexicon validation and five-fold cross-validation reported; released supplementary information and data statements not individually checked.
papers.outcomes: Binary funded/rejected and frequency of promotional terms; no randomized causal outcome, measured readability, merit or actual reviewer comprehension.
limitations: Observational covariate adjustment does not remove unmeasured project merit, reviewer expectations, selection or confounding; author notes need for causal studies (p8).
A dictionary term is not a judgment of exaggeration, truth or appropriateness in context. Their sample substitution examples are sometimes awkward or change intensity.
Five-fold validation reported (Fig 2) without predictive accuracy or independent temporal/external sample evaluation in main paper; does not establish causal or prospective performance.

Page 2 says 38.4% of NNF and 33.7% of NIH are women, with numerators using all applications although phrasing ambiguously follows awarded subset. Treat 3491/9096 and 823/2439 as full-application counts.
NIH sample and one private foundation do not represent other funders, disciplines or eras.
data_or_code_leads: Main paper pages 2, 9–10: NNF data obtainable through cooperative agreement on request; NIH data internal university request; supplement 1 lists dictionary, operationalization, model tables, supplement 2 data statement. Neither supplement inspected; no reproducible repository verified.
extraction_issues: Article uses causal wording ("can increase") but discussion explicitly calls for causal analyses; this review treats estimates as associations. NNF adjusted OR in main results 1.47 while figure 2 shows 1.46. Caption and text disagree about odds versus probability for 53% change.
papers.review_scope: Strategy-use verification of selected decisive passages; specialist review supplies full-paper extraction.

findings.claim: Promotional language is associated with grant success; the paper explicitly calls for causal investigation of mechanisms. Neither blanket deletion nor insertion of promotional words follows.
findings.evidence_locator: Discussion, Limitations and Conclusions: statistical association, future causal analyses, agency scope.
findings.denominator: No new numeric effect estimate in this strategic finding; see specialist record for original study units.
findings.interpretation_limits: Scoped study result or pedagogical implication; not a test of this plugin.

papers.title: In search of commonalities: Some linguistic and rhetorical features of business reports as a genre
papers.study_kind: primarily qualitative descriptive genre corpus study
papers.scope: Authentic internal and external business reports, mainly Hong Kong with Singapore, Malaysia and UK sources, prepared for organizational clients, management, stakeholders or public; not a sample of decision memos per se.
papers.sample_and_design: 22 nonrandom convenience samples submitted by organizations; 12 external and 10 internal, 7 review, 6 problem-solving, 5 market and 4 feasibility reports. Management authors and some collective authorship; writers interviewed where possible, exact interview count not given (PDF pp. 4–6).
papers.outcomes: Observed macro organization, recommendations, rhetorical patterns and lexico-grammar; not independent measurement of decision outcomes or reader comprehension.
limitations: Organizations supplied examples, not random or representative; mostly Hong Kong and medium/large firms. Paper stresses its qualitative size limitation and seeks quantitative replication (pp. 5, 22–23).
19/22 vs only two without explicit recommendation wording is unresolved.
No coder agreement method or downloadable coded dataset identified in full text; example business figures anonymized.
The author claims an inherent implicit recommendation even for sales reports; inference, not a directly observed reader action.
data_or_code_leads: No open coded data or codebook release identified in paper; quotations contain confidential anonymization.
extraction_issues: Observed numbers 19 with clearly stated recommendations and two without explicit recommendations are textually inconsistent; preserve as reported.

papers.title: A move/step model for methods sections: Demonstrating Rigour and Credibility
papers.study_kind: multidisciplinary descriptive corpus and expert-consultation study
papers.scope: Methods sections of IMRD experimental research articles; excludes disciplines whose scholarship differs substantially, such as mathematics, statistics, architecture and history (PDF p. 4).
papers.sample_and_design: 900 texts in 30 disciplines, 30 selected articles per discipline from 3–5 reputable journals; 150 exemplary sections seeded coding; expert-selected recent studies and one consultant per discipline limit representativeness; 1,423,131 words. Human annotations with sentence/phrase units and secondary overlapping functions (PDF pp. 3–6).
papers.outcomes: Functional-semantic move/step inventories and annotated unit frequency, sequences, consultant perceived occurrence, discipline clustering. No direct test of improved writing outcomes.
limitations: One faculty consultant per discipline, purposively selected 30 studies per field, and explicitly excluded non-IMRD disciplinary traditions; no representative prevalence claim.
Paper does not perform full lexico-grammatical realization analysis (PDF p.16).
Unit share vs document presence conflated in author’s optionality label; do not adopt.
One source paragraph misnames Move 2 Step 7 as rationalizing, whereas inventory and definition show Step 6 rationalizing and Step 7 reporting incrementals (PDF pp.9,15).
Original study imposes primary label and secondary label; this project does not require a primary function.
data_or_code_leads: Authors report annotated corpus used through Callisto or other platforms and a move/step functional concordancer (PDF pp.15–16); release URL, data rights, model and corpus files remain unverified.
extraction_issues: Table 3 labels step frequencies sentences; paper elsewhere calls totals functional segments. Report denominator as printed and preserve overlap.

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: skills/write-with-purpose/SKILL.md contribution, voice and standalone reader edit; accepted-foundations.md
proposed_rule_changes.scope_trigger: Substantial writing or a long revision session with supplied author materials
proposed_rule_changes.proposal: Persist original ideas and their provenance, current reader task, structural alternatives and scoped author decisions; retrieve only relevant guidance.
proposed_rule_changes.expected_benefit: Fewer repeated corrections and lost ideas across turns while exposing useful author choices.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A one-sentence copy edit needs no session questionnaire or outline.
proposed_rule_changes.code: Store source roles, exact bytes, decisions and versioned diffs; enforce only actual declared constraints.
proposed_rule_changes.model: Infer tentative structure and ask a consequential missing-content question; propose minimal revisions.
proposed_rule_changes.author: Supply intent, experience and judgment; choose voice and structural route.
proposed_rule_changes.validation: Same-model skills baseline versus harness; measure repair effort, author-recognized meaning and reader task success.

proposed_rule_changes.disposition: refine architecture; reject mandatory exhaustive runtime labeling
proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: Astra candidate revision and rule-calibration report
proposed_rule_changes.scope_trigger: Routine drafting or feedback rather than research annotation
proposed_rule_changes.proposal: Use sparse issue-centered feedback; collect detailed functions/targets only for a consequential ambiguity. Keep realization spans separate from evidence anchors.
proposed_rule_changes.expected_benefit: Lower irrelevant interaction and easier inspection without forced single-function prose.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A function-boundary research study requires complete annotation, including negative and uncertain cases.
proposed_rule_changes.code: Validate recorded anchors and targets, maintain missing/not-collected status.
proposed_rule_changes.model: State concrete reader consequence and alternative; abstain where source context is inadequate.
proposed_rule_changes.author: Keep wording or choose remedy.
proposed_rule_changes.validation: Feedback precision and false alarms, missed material issues, interaction burden; no semantic-success claim from fewer labels.

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: Accepted Family→Form→Section; paragraph functions; dataset-adoption crosswalk
proposed_rule_changes.scope_trigger: Planning a section or inspecting a draft in a known or provisional form
proposed_rule_changes.proposal: Show section jobs and optional functional blanks; preserve source layers and alternate sequences.
proposed_rule_changes.expected_benefit: Author learns available structures without copying source phrasing or normalizing prose toward a median.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A reflective essay may need neither printed headings nor a final resolved lesson.
proposed_rule_changes.code: Preserve original label namespaces, units, spans and source rights.
proposed_rule_changes.model: Explain structural options and tradeoffs appropriate to material.
proposed_rule_changes.author: Choose, combine or replace structure.
proposed_rule_changes.validation: Author can explain selected structure and transfer choice to an unaided task; readers recover intended relation.

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: Technical-term and source-fidelity protections in both current skills
proposed_rule_changes.scope_trigger: A term, condition or assertive phrase creates a real audience or evidence question
proposed_rule_changes.proposal: Protect meaningful terms and certainty while considering explanation in the reading flow; permit truthful positive emphasis rather than vocabulary bans.
proposed_rule_changes.expected_benefit: Preserve precise ideas while reducing avoidable reader difficulty.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: Specialist readers may prefer an exact technical term to a longer everyday paraphrase; a supported novel contribution may deserve assertive wording.
proposed_rule_changes.code: Locate declared terms and changed tokens as review candidates; no semantic entailment claim.
proposed_rule_changes.model: Judge referents, conditions, claim strength and reader assumptions against context.
proposed_rule_changes.author: Confirm intended meaning and tone.
proposed_rule_changes.validation: Independent fidelity review and actual audience task, distinct from perceived ease or award prediction.

proposed_rule_changes.scope_trigger: A source-based style rule or metric is suggested
proposed_rule_changes.proposal: Keep source scope, outcome, trigger, counterexample and check type with the rule. Do not optimize attention, citations, funding or readability unless they are the author-declared objective, and retain fidelity.
proposed_rule_changes.expected_benefit: Prevent descriptive associations becoming universal edits.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: A user may explicitly request a truthful headline experiment with click-through as an outcome.
proposed_rule_changes.code: Resolve provenance, scope metadata and declared limits; no automatic conversion from observations.
proposed_rule_changes.model: Assess applicability and communicate material uncertainty.
proposed_rule_changes.author: Choose objectives and acceptable tradeoffs.
proposed_rule_changes.validation: Audit scope violations and unsupported rule applications on held-out forms.

proposed_rule_changes.existing_rule: Current skills distinguish conformance, correctness and usefulness; calibration limitations
proposed_rule_changes.scope_trigger: Claiming this harness improves writing or learning
proposed_rule_changes.proposal: Test same-model current-skills baseline versus harness on fresh matched author tasks; counterbalance order, separate fidelity/voice/reader performance/burden and unaided transfer.
proposed_rule_changes.expected_benefit: Attribute benefit to harness behavior and identify tradeoffs or harm.
proposed_rule_changes.counterexample: Higher acceptance or lower word count alone can reflect compliance or omission.
proposed_rule_changes.code: Retain assigned conditions, frozen versions, actual usage/timing and reproducible calculations.
proposed_rule_changes.model: Support analysis without acting as sole gold judge.
proposed_rule_changes.author: Judge intended voice and usable outcome; choose meaningful priorities before results.
proposed_rule_changes.validation: Predeclare success criteria; do not treat feasibility pilot as general superiority.
